sources.outlet: Argonne National Laboratory (Lahaina Wildfire Study, ANL-24/65, prepared at FEMA's request)
sources.quote: Within the affected area, 25% of the households were multi-generational households, compared to 9% statewide and 5.5% nationally.
sources.searcher_note: Report dated July 2024, revised October 2024. Covers the three burn tracts incl. 314.04; says doubling up and mixed owner/renter households make pre-fire occupancy hard to pin down, and many foreign-born residents were not eligible for FEMA aid. Context for registrations-per-resident, not the verification rate. PDF text read via local extraction.

sources.outlet: Maui Wildfire Exposure Study (MauiWES), posted by Hawaii DBEDT invest.hawaii.gov
sources.quote: More than 78 percent of Lahaina Front Street participants and 60 percent of Lahainaluna participants reported living in temporary housing.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff report on tracts 314.04 (Lahaina Front Street) and 314.05; names the same tract but measures displacement and hardship in a study cohort, not FEMA occupancy verification. PDF text read via local extraction.

notes: No source found that reports FEMA's occupancy-verification rate for Lahaina registrations, by tract or overall, or the 3,261 registrations vs 3,223 residents in tract 314.04. Coverage found is FEMA process guidance (automated public-records occupancy check, documents to prove occupancy, second homes and vacation rentals ineligible) and housing-program stories, none with verification counts. GAO-25-106862 (Dec 2024, wildfires and FEMA assistance) fetched; its HTML index contained no occupancy-verification sentences. FEMA DR-4724 rumor-response page and the July 2026 monthly fact sheet had no registration or verification figures. Only pattern-adjacent context is recorded.
